description: The named first-person protagonist: an indentured child of the Night Court trained by Anafiel Delaunay as a courtesan and observer, whose investigation, captivity, journey, and political warning drive this novel. Her self-account is preserved as first-person evidence rather than a neutral biography.

power_traditions.note: Fictional divine-mark terminology; no generic power equivalence.

states_and_transformations.note: Content caution: captivity is not consensual service.

metaphysical_laws_and_rituals.note: Fictional religion; no real religious mapping.

canon_status: named central individual in the declared novel

supports: Phèdre narrates her own origin, Night Court upbringing, scarlet mark, and sacred context.
Her Delaunay training, investigation, forced captivity, journey, and political role are narrated.

comparison_cautions: First-person narration limits claims about other characters' inner lives and motives.
Her adult chosen work in Naamah's service must not be conflated with later coercion, enslavement, or sexual violence.
No sequel outcome or later self-understanding is imported.
